acceptance_criteria: A merge the host will not complete (branch protection / required review / not-actually-mergeable) never routes the task into execution/implement rework.
An authorized /approve that branch protection will not honor is surfaced/escalated to the owner with an actionable reason, not silently re-promoted every poll or looped.

The pr_ready_to_merge / /approve-promotion re-entry path is bounded or gated so a promotion that structurally cannot complete cannot loop unbounded (closing the gap max_blocker_reentries does not cover).

Readiness is decided using the host's real 'will this merge?' signal (e.g. GitHub mergeable_state/mergeStateStatus and/or reviewDecision), not just the boolean mergeable, so 'mergeable shape but blocked by protection' is distinguished from 'mergeable and the host will merge'.
A genuinely approved + green + host-will-merge PR still merges automatically with no behavior change (regression preserved).
Host-specific merge-blocked detection lives in the git-hosting plugin behind the adapter contract; the wait/escalate/route policy lives in Core so a second hosting plugin inherits the safety.
A genuine merge conflict (base moved, no longer mergeable) still routes to execution rework as today — the 'blocked merge never reworks' rule does not swallow real conflicts.

The change is covered by unit tests for the blocked-merge routing (poller promotion + auto-merge readiness/failure classification) and the project's gates pass (typecheck, lint, tests). The CI non-final debounce (issue #46) is out of scope.

One contract, both paths: the poller's host-blocked path and auto-merge's host-blocked path resolve the same merge_state=blocked condition to the same task lifecycle state (no longer one blocked-resumable and the other done-terminal).
No false 'completed': the chosen contract does not mark the task successfully done while its PR is still unmerged and undelivered, unless that is a genuine, honest terminal hand-off.

Honest owner-facing message: the message matches what the Engineer can actually do next — it must not promise 'I'll merge it' where the Engineer can never complete the merge; either the block reason is distinguished (required-review-the-owner-can-add vs. Engineer-can-never-merge) and the message branches on it, or the wording holds true in both cases.

A regression test proves both paths (poller escalation + auto-merge readiness/routing) land in the same state for the same host-blocked condition, while the genuine-merge and genuine-conflict regressions still hold and the gates pass.

Optional (not a gate): mapMergeState may switch from a mergeable_state denylist ('blocked' only) to an allowlist (clean/unstable/has_hooks/behind -> mergeable; everything else, e.g. draft, -> hand off) — do only if cheap.
